title: Ops Sentinel: Compact Utility Hub for Runbook-as-Tasks
creator: Luca Moreno
description: Build a compact, embeddable 'Ops Sentinel' utility hub that exposes a minimal API + CLI to run runbooks-as-tasks, surface safe admin utilities, and integrate with the existing telemetry and RBAC stack. Target is to enable first-line support to execute common, audited remediate flows with automatic context collection and a single-step rollback. This is a sprint-scoped engineering initiative to prototype the UX surface and the runtime glue (task dispatch, gating, and telemetry) that can later be extended into the runbook catalog and operator console.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel exposes a /v1/shortflow endpoint that accepts task descriptor, assertions, and run metadata and returns a task_id synchronously.
CLI command `redwood sentinel run <flow>` exists and supports dry-run, audit-only, and execute modes.
Every executed flow emits structured telemetry (trace id, patch id, input snapshot, outcome) visible in Console per-route timeline.
RBAC gating enforced via existing identity service: only users in role 'support-ops' can execute flows that modify infra; audit events persisted to audit-log-storage.
Critical remediations are wrapped with an automatic 2-step canary (dry-run then staged execute) unless explicitly overridden with documented risk reason.
End-to-end tests and a staging PR are merged with green CI and smoke tests validating KV cache safety and idempotency for two example flows.
Design and telemetry owners have reviewed and signed off on the event schema and console visualization contract.
tasks: Define minimal task descriptor schema (inputs, safe-guards, rollback hooks)
Implement HTTP handler + queue-based dispatcher with tag-based routing for dedicated vs hosted execution
Hook into existing RBAC/SSO library to enforce role checks and record principal in audit events
Wire telemetry: create trace/span conventions and log enrichment for Console ingestion
Create two example flows: 'reseed-cache' and 'scale-down-evict' with unit and e2e tests
Draft runbook docs and a shortlisting of safe predicates for ops-exec authors

notes: Design decision: flows are declarative descriptors executed by an idempotent runner; imperative scripts are disallowed for first iteration.
Trade-off: using existing ops-shortflows queue simplifies rollout but couples to current dispatcher semantics — may need adapter for Dedicated mode later.
Follow-ups: create admin UX for previewing telemetry snapshots and add a TTL for stored payloads (30 days default).
